newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB yields still falling despite rock-bottom level.
newsitem.headline: JGB yields still falling despite rock-bottom level.

text.p: Long-term interest rates in Japan are likely to fall further in the near future given the firm demand detected from investors for newly auctioned 10-year government bonds, senior traders said on Wednesday.
The long-term bond yields may stay in a downtrend as long as such buying from investors continues, they said.

"Investors' buying usually emerges after Japan's Golden Week holiday ends. If so, the key bond yield may fall to two percent in May," said Kenichi Hirao, manager in the fixed income division at Sakura Securities.
The key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) was yielding 2.110 percent at noon, against Tuesday's 2.125 finish.
The new 2.4 percent 10-year JGB to be issued in May was priced over par at Tuesday's auction. The coupon rate was cut from 2.5 percent, then a record low, for the April issue.
But the costly May JGB failed to throw cold water on the JGB market.
"We had thought that investors were only interested in bonds with a price under par. But that was not true," said a senior dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage house.
Investors were using JGB futures and interest rate swap (IRS) markets for hedging, a major factor keeping JGB prices from rising sharply, Sakura Securities' Hirao said.
Traders said the JGB market was not "bubbly" as a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official called it last Friday.
"Nobody so far thinks the market is overbought," said Yorinobu Hara, senior deputy general manager in the trading division at Asahi Securities.

"Fears of overbuying may emerge only when the benchmark JGB yield dips below two percent. That may happen in the latter half of May when the market factors in extra cash (of over four trillion yen) emerging in June from maturing JGBs," he said.
Traders said the market is waiting for hard evidence to see if the economy in the April-June quarter was affected by a rise in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.

The key 182nd JGB yield hit an all-time low of 2.075 percent on April 8 after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly tankan corporate survey showed business sentiment at small businesses and non-manufacturers remained sluggish in March and was expected to be the same in June.
Other factors supporting JGB prices include investors' cautiousness in buying other yen bonds than JGBs and weak business sentiment among financial institutions.

"Investors are unnecessarily nervous about credit risks, and this resulted in the JGB yields falling to the lower end of two percent," said Takuma Hayakawa, manager at bond trading division at LTCB Securities.
"If they become aware that there is liquidity risk not only in corporate bonds but in JGBs when interest rates rebound, the JGB yields may stop falling," Hayakawa said.
